I am 58 this year, and I have worked my 8 mu of land for thirty years. I never went to school, but my father and the land itself taught me everything. My household has three mouths to feed. We have a well for irrigation, which means I can water when the rain doesn't come, though the electricity bill always stings.

I run my farm the way I always have: 6 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 2 mu in cotton. The grain keeps us from going hungry and gives us something to sell; the cotton brings in cash for medicine, clothes, and my grandson's school supplies.

My wheat went into the ground last October. Now it is waking up. I will spread urea when it turns green, and I will run the pump three times this spring — green-up, jointing, and when the grain is filling. Wheat is thirsty at those stages, and I know from thirty years that skipping an irrigation costs more in lost yield than the electricity costs. I'll spray twice for aphids and rust. I buy improved wheat seeds from the township supply store — not the cheapest, but they give me about 450 kg per mu, which is honest.

Come June, as soon as the wheat comes off, I plant hybrid maize on those same 6 mu. There is no time to plough — I seed right into the wheat stubble and put fertilizer down with the seeder. Hybrid maize grows fast if you give it water. I irrigate three times: when it is knee-high, when the tassels come out, and when the grain is filling. Two sprays are enough if you time them right. I expect 550 kg per mu.

My cotton is on the other 2 mu. I rotary till it in April and plant hybrid Bt cotton. Cotton needs patience. I put compound fertilizer in the furrows and top-dress with urea when it flowers. Cotton drinks a lot when the bolls are setting, so I irrigate three times, and I spray four times because aphids and red spider mites love cotton, Bt or no Bt. I give it extra potassium because the bolls need it; I learned that twenty years ago when my bolls wouldn't open properly. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer prices have gone up, but I don't cut blindly. I use about 35–40 jin of fertilizer per mu for grain, and a bit more potassium for cotton. That is what works. I don't need a book to tell me — my eyes and my hands know.
